Can fail if truncation removes exploration that would have corrected an early wrong answer, lowering score on ambiguous questions. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Agent Safety Harnesses with Adaptive Injection Stressors
item.description: The method replaces manual, static design of safety harnesses for tool-using agents with automated evolutionary search that optimizes executable harness code against utility and attack-success objectives. It costs significant inference compute for the tree-search evolution loop (using API models or a local evaluator model) plus engineering effort to set up benchmarks, evaluators, and stressor evolution, and it adds a harness layer that affects runtime behavior. It can fail through overfitting to the specific benchmark and attack distribution, degraded protection on harder benchmarks (attack success remains 62.0% on Agent-SafetyBench), regression under adaptive attackers who evolve against the fixed harness, and utility loss if the harness blocks legitimate instructions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: The Between-Round Decision in Autonomous Research: An LLM Controller That Reads the Whole Trajectory
item.description: Replaces rule-based, score-based, or search-tree controllers in autonomous research loops with a single LLM call that reads full trajectory history to decide whether to refine the current champion or start a new direction. Costs one additional LLM inference per experimental round plus the context window capacity to hold accumulated evidence, which grows with trajectory length. Can fail when the trajectory history exceeds effective context limits, when the LLM misjudges which past solution to build from, or when the domain lacks clear verified metrics for the controller to ground its decisions. 1 independent implementation, 130 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CrossEnv: Synthesizing Verifiable Cross-Environment Tasks for Long-Horizon Agent Training
item.description: The method replaces hand-curated, single-environment agent training tasks with automatically synthesized cross-environment tasks built on an entity-tool graph, combined with a curriculum that scales from single-environment tool use to multi-service coordination. The cost is the engineering effort required to construct and maintain the entity-tool graph, align cross-environment data for executability and verifiability, and generate sufficient synthetic task volume, which is non-trivial for a small team. Failure modes include data inconsistency across environments breaking task verifiability, synthetic task distribution mismatch with real production workloads reducing transfer, and the graph construction becoming a bottleneck as new services or APIs are added. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Passing Checks Do Not Establish Completion: Evidence Interpretation in Coding Agents
item.description: The technique replaces ad-hoc verification in coding agents with qualified repository checks and controlled evidence consumers to ensure execution facts are preserved and obligations discharged. It costs added workflow complexity for receipts, repairs, and lifetime controls without requiring extra hardware or training. Passing checks may fail to establish completion if facts are misreported or scope is exceeded, limiting diagnostic superiority. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
item.description: SCoRe replaces summary-based continuation by compacting context at stop bursts and marking impossibility judgments as unproven. It costs the compute and latency of extended agent execution up to thousands of turns, plus the complexity of managing context summaries. It can fail by consuming excessive API budget or context window on unproductive tasks without yielding further verified gains. 0 independent implementations, 2134 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Born for the Task: Rethinking Quantum Chemistry with Foresighted Agentic Computing
item.description: BORN replaces hand-configured general-purpose quantum chemistry packages with coding agents that synthesize task-specific high-performance programs, selecting algorithmic components from a predicted accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier before execution. It costs an agent-driven synthesis phase plus the infrastructure to extrapolate error from small systems and measure hardware throughputs, and the headline gains are estimated against baselines rather than measured end-to-end. Adoption can fail if small-system error extrapolation mispredicts target-scale accuracy, if runtime prediction misses actual hardware behavior, or if the reader's workloads lie outside the demonstrated Hartree-Fock-style calculations. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Done, But Still Working: Anytime Evaluation of When Coding Agents Should Stop
item.description: The method replaces letting coding agents run until their self-imposed termination by replaying recorded runs, scoring intermediate patches with hidden tests, and applying stopping or earlier-patch-selection rules. It costs evaluation infrastructure for anytime replay with hidden tests and, for the fine-tuning variant, a training pipeline; the stopping rules themselves are cheap heuristics. Adoption can fail because the preregistered quality test does not establish non-inferiority: stopping early may discard patch changes that would have repaired the solution, and savings vary sharply by model and scaffold. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling
item.description: The technique replaces unconditional full re-rendering and blocking build-check-render pipelines in code-to-video agent workflows with a training-free execution layer that caches frames by drawing commands and runs checks before rendering at idle priority. It costs additional CPU for speculative rendering that may be discarded when checks fail, plus the complexity of integrating an execution layer behind existing agent commands. It can fail when frame keys miss due to genuinely new content, when recent build history mispredicts check outcomes and wastes render compute, and in domains where the agent's edits rarely produce reusable frames. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SEAM: Computer-Use Agents Know the Harm Between Screens, and Commit It Anyway
item.description: SEAM replaces single-screen safety benchmarks by testing cross-screen compositional harm detection in computer-use agents. It costs minimal infrastructure as it relies on server-log scoring and pre-built tasks, though integration into existing CI/CD pipelines requires engineering effort. However, agents may pass the benchmark by relying on user instruction cues without robust reasoning when facts are presented separately. 1 independent implementation, 2135 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: PhysScope: Agentic Multimodal Physics Reasoning with Grounded Visual Memory
item.description: It replaces direct VLM solving and visual chain-of-thought (e.g., Canvas-CoT) with an inference-time harness that registers physical scopes, constructs derived views, and invalidates dependent claims on revision, without weight updates. Cost is extra inference calls, generated derived views, and bookkeeping of a scope-aware working memory, increasing latency and orchestration complexity while remaining API-compatible. It can fail when proposed revisions or scope links are themselves wrong, when dependent invalidation is incomplete, and the reported gains may not transfer beyond physics-diagram reasoning. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Values Shape What Self-Improving Coding Agents Build
item.description: The method replaces value-neutral persistent instruction files in self-improving coding agents with short human-written value statements (from Schwartz's higher-order value types) that steer both what the agent builds and how it performs. It costs little in memory, latency, or infrastructure, since it is only an instruction-file change, but it adds a design step that the paper shows cannot be delegated: agent-revised values converge and AI-literature-derived values give no detectable gain. It can fail if the wrong value set is chosen (conservation values degraded performance below baseline) and requires workload-specific validation plus continued human oversight of value design. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Dynamic Task Allocation with Dialogue
item.description: Replaces static or purely LLM-driven task allocation with a probabilistic framework that uses dialogue to reduce uncertainty in multi-agent coordination. Costs include maintaining explicit belief states, implementing structured communication protocols, and added decision and coordination overhead. It can fail if belief models are misspecified, dialogue is unreliable or misinterpreted, or the environment is too dynamic for the Bayesian updates to remain accurate. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Inference after coding agents
item.description: The method replaces uncorrected classical inference after agent-driven data analysis with a post-hoc replay procedure: reset the agent on subsamples of the data to estimate the probability it would select the reported analysis when it is statistically favorable, then adjust the test conditional on selection. The cost is substantial additional agent compute (multiple black-box replays per analysis, which scales with API or GPU budget) plus engineering to snapshot and replay the exact agent environment; statistical validity requires that the agent's selection behavior be stable across replays. It can fail if the agent's behavior is non-deterministic, drifts between runs, depends on unreplayable state, or if the subsample design does not approximate the original selection process; nominal coverage is only guaranteed asymptotically and conditional on stable selection. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.
